newsitem.title: UK: Falling stocks drive LME copper up, eyes $2,000.
newsitem.headline: Falling stocks drive LME copper up, eyes $2,000.

text.p: Copper prices came within a whisker of breaking above the key psychological $2,000-a-tonne barrier on Thursday on the London Metal Exchange (LME), but again ran into selling near the level.
Aluminium finished above previous resistance at $1,420 while other metals moved in tandem with market leaders copper and aluminium in fairly thin volumes, traders and analysts said.
"For the moment the short-term fundamentals which we can see are obviously supportive of higher prices," said Angus MacMillan, analyst at Billiton Metals.
"Selling above the market will cap any rally...but sellers may back off a bit while this strength continues," he added.
Benchmark three month copper futures finished the afternoon kerb at $1,993 a tonne, up $17 from Wednesday's afternoon close.
Floor dealers said prices rose in anticipation of another sizeable drawdown in LME stocks on Friday, and physical traders said market fundamentals were bullish in the short term.

Material was going to end-users in Europe and the Middle East as well as to Chinese stocks in Shanghai, the traders said. Only some of the 40,000 tonnes or so of copper destined for China would move back to LME Singapore warehouses, some added.
LME copper stocks have fallen over 115,000 tonnes in less than two months and are not far above the low point of 141,100 reached in July 1995.

While stocks were low and expected to fall further, doubts remained over the market's upside potential. Producer selling, long liquidation and short position holders protecting their positions were all bearish factors in the market, traders said.

Aluminium rose $19 to $1,424 on short-covering and institutional buying. Producer selling emerged around midday to depress values, but buying picked up again during the afternoon session to lift the market above the chart point at $1,420.

Unconfirmed trade talk of a meeting between Canadian and Russian officials scheduled for Friday to discuss ways of addressing persistent low prices was lending some background support, traders and analysts said.
Chartists said the bullish close could signal a move to $1,440 soon. But much would depend on Friday's stock data, traders added.
Most other base metals followed swings in copper and aluminium. Nickel gained $55 to $7,230 while zinc rose $2.50 to $1,027. Lead edged up $2 to $737 and alloy moved to $1,280 from $1,270.
Tin was the only metal to buck the trend, nudging lower by $5 to $5,980 by the close.
